source_query: SELECT executive_summary, created_at FROM uc13_ale.analysis.diligence_report WHERE company_name = 'Elder Care' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1

claims.claim_text: Elder Care Homecare is a private-pay home care company operating across six locations in the Tri-State region (NY, NJ, CT, and MA).
The company generates revenue by billing private-pay clients for caregiver hours delivered.
Elder Care had approximately 352 active clients as of Q2 2025.
Elder Care had 2,123 registered caregivers across markets including NYC, Long Island, Westchester, NJ, MA, and CT as of Q2 2025.
The platform completed at least two transactions — Guided Living and Unicity — within the recent historical window.
Elder Care is currently ramping a Connecticut de novo location.
Pro Forma Adjusted Revenue reached $46.4M on a TTM Aug-24 basis per the Historical P&L Summary workstream.
Revenue grew from $8,955K in 2020A to $46,423K TTM Aug-24.
Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDA was $9,239K representing a 19.9% margin on a pro forma basis.
Reported (pre-addback) EBITDA margin is approximately 7.9%, below the ~10% healthcare services threshold.
The addback schedule contains 17 discrete Tier 4 items totaling approximately $7.3M in gross adjustments.
Gross addbacks represent approximately 247% of reported EBITDA.
Every addback item has been classified Tier 4 because no supporting documents are referenced in the addback schedule within the VDR.
Run-rate executive compensation addback is $2,490K.
Unicity pre-acquisition results addback is $1,077K.
Unicity synergies addback is $909K.
The reconciliation workstream flagged one mismatch and was unable to verify nine items.
The forecast projects revenue growing from $47.2M (2024E) to $197.8M (2029P) — a 4.2x increase.
The Forecast workstream rates the five-year revenue trajectory Red given aggressive assumptions.
The company received adverse NYSDOH survey citations in May 2023 related to HCR Profile maintenance, background-check consent procedures, and Home Care Registry credentialing timelines.
Written DOH confirmation of closure of the May 2023 NYSDOH citations has not been confirmed.
Verification that no agreements exist with OIG/SAM-excluded individuals or entities has not been cleared.
Outside counsel was retained as recently as April 30, 2025 to pursue collection of patient receivables.
The Manhattan office lease contains an anti-assignment covenant that may require landlord consent as a closing condition.
Overall analytical confidence across all seven workstreams is rated Medium.
Five of seven workstreams carry at least one Red or Yellow rating on a material dimension.
Elder Care operates zero Medicare-certified or Medicaid-reimbursed locations.
The Quality of Earnings workstream validated every Tier 4 addback against audited standalone financials.
Elder Care provides home health aide, live-in, and nursing services to elderly patients.
The platform has grown both organically and through acquisition.
The reported EBITDA base is roughly $7.7M.
Cash-to-accrual revenue adjustment addback is $665K.
Guided Living ramp-up adjustment addback is $430K.
Each of the five largest individual addbacks individually exceeds 5% of reported EBITDA.

The five largest addbacks include forward-looking pro forma synergies and pre-close acquisition earnings that have not been validated against audited standalone financials or demonstrated post-close performance.
If even a portion of these addbacks are rejected in a buyer QofE, the defensible EBITDA base could approach zero or turn negative, fundamentally altering valuation and leverage capacity.
Forecast revenue growth is driven by organic growth, the Connecticut de novo ramp, and additional expansion.
The diligence process has surfaced several critical and material issues across workstreams.
Corrective action plans and the absence of ongoing monitoring obligations for the NYSDOH citations have not been confirmed.
Potential False Claims Act exposure from OIG/SAM exclusion screening has not been cleared.
The addback stack's composition — including speculative forward synergies and unaudited pre-close acquisition earnings — represents the single most consequential open item for price and structure.
Patient receivables collection activity raises questions about billing integrity and working capital quality.
Material customer contracts contain termination-for-convenience provisions whose interaction with a change-of-control has not been confirmed.
Two identified clients show significant multi-year billing declines whose treatment in the run-rate revenue base has not been clarified.
Unusual indemnity provisions appear across multiple contracts including the Unicity Asset Purchase Agreement.
Five of seven workstreams carry a Red rating (Financial Trends, KPI, Legal Contracts, Quality of Earnings, and Forecast).
Two workstreams are rated Yellow (Business Model, Customer Quality).
Open item 1: seller-provided audited or third-party-verified support is required for each of the 17 Tier 4 addbacks, with particular focus on the five items individually exceeding 5% of EBITDA.
Open item 2: written DOH confirmation of regulatory citation closure and a completed OIG/SAM exclusion screening for all employees, contractors, and vendors are required.
Open item 3: quantification and aging of receivables in active legal collection are required.
Open item 4: confirmation is required of whether material customer contracts contain change-of-control triggers.
Open item 5: location-level P&L and operational KPIs for Guided Living, Unicity, ECHC, and the Connecticut de novo are required to validate the entity-level EBITDA build-up.
The Legal Contracts workstream should engage outside counsel to confirm whether the Manhattan lease anti-assignment provision applies to the contemplated transaction structure.
